mainEntity.name: How long does a dental crown typically last before it needs replacing?

acceptedAnswer.text: The lifespan of a dental crown varies depending on the material, its location in the mouth, and individual patient habits. Many crowns function well for ten to fifteen years or longer. However, wear, changes in the bite, gum recession, or underlying tooth problems may require earlier replacement in some cases. Regular dental check-ups allow your dentist to monitor the condition of your crown and advise you on its longevity based on your specific situation.

mainEntity.name: Can a worn crown cause damage to the opposing tooth?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, in some circumstances. Certain crown materials — particularly rough or unglazed ceramic surfaces — can cause wear to the opposing natural tooth if they are excessively hard or abrasive. This is one reason why material selection and regular monitoring are important aspects of crown treatment. Your dentist will check for signs of wear on both the crowned tooth and the opposing teeth during routine examinations.

mainEntity.name: Is sensitivity in a crowned tooth always a sign that something is wrong?

acceptedAnswer.text: Not necessarily. Some sensitivity following crown placement is normal and usually settles within a few weeks. However, new or worsening sensitivity in a tooth that has had a crown for some time may indicate that the crown's seal has been compromised, that wear has thinned the material, or that there is an underlying issue with the tooth itself. If sensitivity persists or is troubling you, it is worth discussing with your dentist.

mainEntity.name: Can teeth grinding be treated to protect my crown?

acceptedAnswer.text: Bruxism cannot always be fully resolved, as its causes are often multifactorial and may be related to stress, sleep patterns, or jaw alignment. However, its impact on crowns and natural teeth can be significantly reduced with a custom-made occlusal splint worn during sleep. Your dentist may also explore other contributing factors and refer you for further assessment where appropriate. Treatment suitability depends on individual clinical assessment.

mainEntity.name: Will I know if my crown has started to wear down?

acceptedAnswer.text: Not always. Early wear may not cause noticeable symptoms, which is one of the reasons why routine dental examinations are valuable. A dentist can identify wear patterns using clinical examination and, where needed, dental radiographs — before significant problems develop. If you have any concerns about your crown between appointments, do not hesitate to contact your dental practice.

mainEntity.name: Is it safe to delay replacing a worn crown?

acceptedAnswer.text: The appropriateness of timing for crown replacement depends on several clinical factors, including the degree of wear, the integrity of the marginal seal, and the condition of the underlying tooth and surrounding tissues. Your dentist will advise you on whether monitoring, minor intervention, or prompt replacement is most appropriate. Delaying assessment when symptoms are present is generally not advisable, as underlying issues may progress over time.
